question: What is the primary architectural advantage of programming to an interface or superclass reference type in Java?

options.text: Constructors automatically dispatch polymorphically to instantiate the most derived subclass available in memory.
Client code can operate on new subclasses or implementations seamlessly without requiring changes or recompilation.
Downcasting an object transforms its physical heap layout into the destination subtype and reorganizes its internal fields.
Polymorphic behavior is only permitted when every single class in the inheritance chain implements an interface explicitly.

explanation: Runtime polymorphism allows client code written against an abstract supertype to manipulate objects of any current or future subtype uniformly.

question: What does the `instanceof` operator evaluate in the expression `ref instanceof SubType`?

options.text: Whether ref can be cast to SubType without creating a new heap object in the current virtual machine.
Whether the constructor of SubType has been executed in the current thread stack during initialization.
Whether the actual object referenced at runtime is an instance of SubType or one of its subtypes.
The declared compile-time type of the variable ref assigned in the original source code declaration.

explanation: The instanceof operator queries the actual runtime class of the referenced object in memory to test compatibility with the target type.

question: What occurs at runtime when a program attempts an invalid downcast, such as casting an Object reference holding a String into an Integer?

options.text: The JVM throws a ClassCastException at runtime upon verifying the incompatible types.
The compiler issues a static type incompatibility error and halts bytecode compilation immediately.
The JVM parses the string contents into an equivalent integer value and stores it into the destination variable.
The target reference is assigned null automatically without throwing any runtime exception at all.

explanation: Attempting to cast an object to a type outside its actual class hierarchy causes the JVM to throw ClassCastException at runtime.

question: Which of the following statements accurately characterizes polymorphism in Java?

options.text: Downcasting creates a new modified copy of the object containing subclass fields.
Polymorphism requires interfaces; concrete classes cannot exhibit polymorphic dispatch.
The instanceof test is evaluated at compile time and never checks runtime types.
A supertype reference can point to any subclass instance, enabling dynamic invocation of overridden methods.

explanation: Polymorphism enables a supertype reference to point to instances of any subtype and dispatch methods according to the actual runtime class.
